inputs.sequence_prompt:
One continuous fifteen-second live-action shot starting exactly from the provided frame. Stationary tripod camera keeps this single view of the real wooden airship deck, the stone theatre on the left, the cabin and existing stairs on the right. Preserve the three actors, their exact faces, proportions, costumes, existing props, the fixed warm lantern light and the blue-hour sky. The ship and gangway remain docked and motionless throughout.
The silver-haired man Setzer is supported on the existing staircase at right, turned back toward the other two. The blonde woman Celes in the ivory gown and blue sash stands at center. The brown-haired man Locke with the blue bandana stands at left, holding one wooden shield low in his LEFT hand; his sword remains sheathed. The existing rigid wooden X-braced gate panel is swung aside in the lower-left foreground. It must close the access gap beside it. Only these three actors are present.
During the opening three seconds Setzer looks directly toward Locke and says one short instruction in a calm mature male voice, natural Brazilian Portuguese, with synchronized lips: <d>[Portuguese] Feche o portão, Locke.</d> Celes and Locke listen silently. Locke first looks at the existing gate, then turns his shoulders and hips toward it. Celes takes one small grounded step toward the cabin at right, clearing his working space, and watches his hands.
From the third to the tenth second Locke takes a short step beside the free end of the EXISTING gate, remaining on the ship side of the threshold. He keeps his shield close to his left thigh and uses only his free RIGHT hand to grasp the gate's solid top rail. With his boots planted on the deck he smoothly guides this same rigid panel around its original hinges across the open access gap. The panel follows one continuous arc. Its original X braces, top rail, hinge side and dimensions stay fixed. Locke steps with the panel as needed, keeping his torso, knees and shield entirely outside the wooden panel's swept path. The panel reaches the existing opposite post and stops against it. No one passes through the gate or the railing. Celes watches the closing edge, ready to depart. Setzer waits on his supported stair tread until the gate is shut.
During the final five seconds Locke uses his right hand to secure the existing latch, gives the closed top rail one short deliberate tug to verify it stays shut, then releases his hand. Only after the latch holds does he look up toward Setzer and give one clear nod. Setzer acknowledges, turns toward the upper deck and resumes climbing the remaining EXISTING stairs, one boot planted on a wooden tread before the next lifts. His coat follows his legs; the staircase stays rigid. Celes turns her head to follow him, with a quiet breath of relief. End with the gate closed, Locke beside it with his shield still in his left hand, and Setzer moving up toward the command position. Keep the complete action continuous and alive, at normal speed.
Audio contains exactly the single Portuguese sentence above, followed by quiet wind, cloth, separate wooden boot contacts, a low hinge creak and one latch click at the visible contact. No other speech, narration, singing or score. Preserve the one fixed camera view, the original three bodies and physically connected action throughout. The gangway and theatre remain stationary; takeoff has not begun.
